अथापि कृपणं मानुगृहाण वर-दानतः ॥

बतेति हर्षे । हे ईड्य ! नोऽस्माभिः समग्र-सत्त्व-निधेस् तव दर्शनाद् अद्याक्ष्णोः सांसिद्ध्यं साफल्यं जुष्टं सेवितम् । त्वद्-दर्शनम् एव महा-फलम् इत्य् उपपादयति । यस्य तव दर्शनं सद्भिर् उत्तरोत्तरम् आपादित-प्रकर्षैर् जन्मभी रूढो विरूढो योगो यैस् तेऽपि ॥१३॥

entries.literal_english: “I who criticize those with desires am myself just like that,” he says with “tathā.” “Gṛhamedha” means household life. Wishing to marry a wife who, like a cow, yields the three aims of life, I have come to the root—Your feet—of the wish-fulfilling tree that grants every desire. One might ask, “Why not worship something else for desires and the like?” No: You alone are the root of every human aim.

entries.literal_english: “Then why do you not worship solely for liberation?”—because you are not qualified, he says. “O Lord of lords, You are Prajāpati; by Your command this world, struck by desire, is bound like an animal. entries.sanskrit: अनिमिषायेत्य् अनेन कालात्मकात् त्वत्तो भीतः कर्म करोमीत्य् उक्तम् । एतत् तु भयं त्वद्-भक्तानां नास्तीत्य् आह द्वाभ्याम् । लोकान् कामाभिभूतांस् तान् अनुसृतान् पशूंश् च । विवेके सत्य् अपि पुनः कर्म-जडान् मादृशान् हित्वा अनादृत्य ये तव चरण-रूपम् आतपत्रं श्रिताः, तान् एवाह---त्वद्-गुणानां वादः कथा, तद् एव सीधु मदिरा, संसार-विस्मारकत्वात् । पीयूषं रुचि-करत्वात् । तेन निर्यापिता विलापिता देह-धर्माः क्षुत्-पिपासादयो यैः, एषाम् इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: अनिमिषायेत्य् अनेन कालात्मकात् त्वत्तो भीतः कर्म करोमीत्य् उक्तम्
by “for the Unblinking One,” he says, “I act out of fear of You, who are time personified”

having abandoned them, he speaks of those who have taken shelter of the umbrella that is Your feet

those by whom bodily conditions such as hunger and thirst have been cast off through it are the people referred to next
entries.literal_english: By saying “for the Unblinking One,” he has said, “I act out of fear of You, who are time personified.” He says in two verses that this fear does not exist for Your devotees. The people overwhelmed by desire, their followers, and animals; even those who possess discernment but, like me, are dull in action—having abandoned them, those who have taken shelter of the umbrella that is Your feet are described. The discourse on Your qualities is a story; it is wine because it makes one forget worldly existence, and nectar because it is delightful. Those who have been made to cast off bodily conditions such as hunger and thirst by that [story] are the people referred to next.

entries.sanskrit: तव  यत् त्रिणाभि काल-चक्रं, तज् जगद् आच्छिद्य आकृष्य धावद् अपि एषां त्वद्-भक्तानाम् आयुर् आच्छिद्य धावन् न भवति । कथं भूतम् ? अजरं ब्रह्म तस्मिन्न् अक्ष-रूपे भ्रमिर् भ्रमणम् । भ्रमद् इति वक्तव्येऽतिभ्रमण-शीलत्वाद् उपचारेण भ्रमिर् इत्य् अभेद-निर्देशः । अधिक-मासेन सह त्रयोदश मासा अरा यस्य । त्रि-शतं षष्टिश् चाहो-रात्राः पर्वाणि यस्य । शत-शब्दे विभक्तेर् अलुग् आर्षः । षड् ऋतवो नेमयो यस्य । अनन्ताः क्षण-लवादयश् छदाः पत्राणि पत्राकारा धाराः सन्ति यस्य । त्रीणि चातुर्मास्यानि नाभय आधार-भूतानि वलयानि यस्य । कराल-स्रोतस् तीव्र-वेगम् । एतैर् विशेषणैर् एव संवत्सरात्मकं चक्रम् उक्तम् इति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥१८॥

these descriptions are to be understood as specifying the wheel that is the year
entries.literal_english: Your three-naved wheel of time, while running, cuts through and draws along the universe, but it does not cut off the lifespan of these devotees. How is it constituted? Brahman is undecaying; the rotation is on its axle. “Bhrami” is used figuratively for “revolving,” by an identity of expression that conveys exceptionally rapid rotation. It has thirteen spokes, with the intercalary month; its joints are the three hundred and sixty days and nights; its rims are the six seasons; its leaves, or leaf-shaped blades, are the endless moments and instants; its three hubs are the supporting circles of the three four-month seasons. It has a terrible, swift current. These descriptions are to be understood as specifying the wheel that is the year.

entries.sanskrit: ननु निरुपाधिम् उदासीनं मां किं याचसे ? तथापि मायया विश्व-सृष्ट्य्-आदि-कर्तृत्वात् त्वम् एव याच्यः । इत्य् आह---स्वयम् एक एव सन्न् अप्य् आत्मन्य् अधिकृतया योग-मायया हेतु-भूतया याः स्वी-कृताः शक्तयः सत्त्वाद्याः, ताभिः । अदो विश्वम् । स्व-व्यतिरिक्त-साधनानपेक्षत्वे दृष्टान्तः---यथेति ॥१९॥

entries.literal_english: “Why do you ask me, who am without limiting adjuncts and detached?” Even so, since by māyā You perform the creation of the universe and the rest, You alone are to be asked. He says: although You alone exist, the powers such as sattva, which You have assumed within Yourself through yogamāyā acting as their cause, bring about this universe. “As” gives an example of not needing an instrument separate from oneself.

entries.sanskrit: यद्य् अपि मायिकत्वाद् भक्तेभ्यो विषय-सुखं दातुं नेच्छसि, तथाप्य् अस्मद्-अभिप्रायानुसारेण तत् संपादय, इत्य् आह---नैतद् इति । हे अधीश ! नोऽस्माकं भजतां भूत-सूक्ष्म-रूपं पदं शब्दादि-विषय-सुखं मायया तनुषे विस्तारयसीति । यद् एतत् तव यद्य् अपि ईप्सितं न भवति, तथाप्य् अस्मद्-अनुग्रहायास् तु, ऋण-त्रयापाकरणानन्तरम् एवापवर्गाय भवत्व् इत्य् अर्थः । यर्हि यतो मायया परिच्छिन्न इव लसन्त्या तुलस्या युक्तस् त्वं विलक्षितोऽसि । एवं-भूतस्य तव दर्शनं यतो भुक्ति-मुक्ति-प्रदम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२०॥

एवं-भूतस्य तव दर्शनं यतो भुक्ति-मुक्ति-प्रदम् इत्य् अर्थः
the vision of You in this form grants both enjoyment and liberation; this is the meaning
entries.literal_english: “Although, because it is māyic, You may not wish to give sense-pleasure to Your devotees, nevertheless fulfill it in accordance with our intention,” he says with “naitad.” “O Lord, You do not expand for us, Your worshipers, through māyā the subtle-element state that is the basis of sense pleasures such as sound.” Although this may not be what You desire, let it be for Your favor to us; after the three debts have been discharged, may it lead to liberation. Since You are seen, joined with Tulasī, shining as though bounded by māyā, this vision of You grants both enjoyment and liberation.

entries.sanskrit: तं त्वा त्वां भुक्ति-मुक्ति-प्रदं नमामि । मुक्ति-दत्वे हेतुः, अनुभूत्या ज्ञानेनोपरतः क्रियार्थः कर्म-फल-भोगो यस्मिन् । भोग-दत्वे हेतुः, स्व-मायया आवर्तितं लोक-तन्त्रं विश्वोपकरणं येन । अतः स-कामैर् निष्कामैश् च नमनीयं पाद-सरोजं यस्य तम् । तत्राल्पीयसि स-कामे पुंसि भजने वा कामान् वर्षतीति तथा तम् ॥२१॥

entries.literal_english: I bow to You, who bestow both enjoyment and liberation. As the giver of liberation, You are the one in whom action directed toward its fruit is brought to rest through knowledge born of experience. As the giver of enjoyment, by Your own māyā You set in motion the order of the world, the instrument of the universe. Therefore Your lotus feet are to be bowed to by those with desires and by those without them. For a person with only a small desire, or in a modest act of worship, You are one who rains down the desired objects.

entries.sanskrit: अशेषैस्  तपो-मन्त्रादि-सिद्धेश्वरैर् अभिष्टुतः सिद्ध-मार्गो वैकुण्ठ-मार्गो यस्य । यद् वा, अशेष-सिद्धेश्वराभिष्टुतश् चासौ सिद्धैर् मृग्यत इति सिद्ध-मार्गश् च स ययौ । पत्र-रथेन्द्रो गरुडस् तस्य पक्षैर् उदीर्णम् अभिव्यक्तं साम आकर्णयन्, बृहद्-रथान्तरे पक्षौ इति श्रुतेः । उच्चारितं स्तोमं च सामाधार-भूताणाम् ऋचां समुदायं शृण्वन् । स्तोम आत्मा इति श्रुतेः । समास-पाठे उच्चारितः स्तोमः स्तोत्रीय-समुदायो यस्य साम्न इति ॥३४॥

since the Śruti says that the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are his wings

and hearing the pronounced stoma, the collection of Ṛks that form the basis of the Sāmans

समास-पाठे उच्चारितः स्तोमः स्तोत्रीय-समुदायो यस्य साम्न इति
in the compound recitation, “pronounced stoma” means the collection of stotṛ verses belonging to the Sāman
entries.literal_english: His path is praised by all accomplished masters of austerity, mantra, and the rest: the perfected path is the road to Vaikuṇṭha. Or, he himself is praised by all accomplished lords, and he went along the perfected path sought by the siddhas. While listening to the Sāman song made manifest by the wings of Garuḍa, king of birds—since the Śruti says that the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are his wings—and hearing the pronounced stoma, the collection of Ṛks that form the basis of the Sāmans. The Śruti says, “the stoma is the self.” In the compound recitation, “pronounced stoma” means the collection of stotṛ verses belonging to the Sāman.

जैत्रं जय-प्रदं मणि-गणा अर्पिता यस्मिंस् तं रथम् आरुह्य त्वं यदा भुवो मण्डलं न पर्यटसि तदा सेतवो भिद्येरन्न् इति त्रयाणाम् अन्वयः
“jaitra” means victory-giving; the chariot is adorned with a row of gems. The syntax is: “When You do not travel around the circle of the earth mounted on that chariot, the bridges would break”
विस्फूर्जन्-नादं कुर्व-चण्डं कोदण्डं धनुर् यस्य
He whose bow makes a fierce, resounding sound
वर्णाश्रमाणां निबन्धनं यैः
“those by whom the social and spiritual orders are established”
बत अहो
“bata” means “ah!”
entries.literal_english: This is the meaning of the five verses beginning “na yadet”: “Although Your coming may be occasioned by Your roaming everywhere to protect dharma, nevertheless, if there is a special task, please state it.” “Jaitra” means victory-giving; the chariot is adorned with a row of gems. The syntax of three verses is: “When You do not travel around the circle of the earth mounted on that chariot, the bridges would break.” He whose bow makes a fierce, resounding sound; “those by whom the social and spiritual orders are established”; “bata” means “ah!”
